summary: A humorous collection of family cooking mishaps from households across the U.S., each tied to a beloved comfort food recipe and a specific date between September 2023 and October 2024. Stories include misread measurements, a spilled gravy boat, a flopped upside-down cake, a dog stealing dumplings, an overly spicy chili, and an overgrown loaf. The piece concludes that family gatherings thrive on imperfection, laughter, and togetherness.
one_line: A lighthearted roundup of U.S. families' comfort-food kitchen disasters, from salty mac 'n' cheese to a runaway loaf, celebrating togetherness.
key_facts: Sally Hamilton of Topeka, Kansas guards the family recipe box, whose grandmother's apple pie recipe calls for "a dash of love and a smidge of patience."

On October 17, 2023, Aunt Mabel's potluck nearly became 'Name That Casserole' when the family tried to decipher her scribbled beef bourguignon card; 12-year-old Timmy joked it should simmer "an hour, not a year."
In November 2023, Sharon O'Connor of Poughkeepsie's sons misread "tsp" as "tbsp" for salt in her mac 'n' cheese, creating "Mac 'n' Cheese á la Dead Sea" per Uncle Joe's remark.
On September 12, 2023, Elmer Jenkins of Little Rock, Arkansas had his barbecue sauce altered when granddaughter Suzie secretly added grape soda; her brother Jim asked if Pa put grape jelly in it.
On November 23, 2023, the Wilkins family of Portland, Oregon lost their Thanksgiving gravy when Uncle Fred knocked the gravy boat off the counter; Cousin Linda called it a "gravy train wreck."
On September 30, 2023, Betty Morgan of Cleburne, Texas flipped a pineapple upside-down cake and the pineapple slices fell out of formation, so the family ate 'Pineapple Right-Side-Up cake.'
On February 3, 2024, during Lunar New Year, a batch of the Lee family's dumplings in San Francisco vanished; their Shih Tzu, Lucky, was found with a round belly and the last dumpling.
In October 2024, the Gonzalez family of El Paso, Texas held a chili cook-off where a teenager added too much cayenne pepper; the dish became known as 'Chili Con Flagrante.'
On April 13, 2024, the Baker family of Breadville, Ohio had their loaf's yeast over-expand; son Michael joked, "It's not a loaf, it's an uprising!"
The Hamilton recipe box is described as a worn cardboard box with a faded mural of apples and cinnamon sticks.
After the salt mishap, the O'Connor family invested in larger, legible measuring spoons.
The Jenkins family's barbecue now comes with an optional side of grape soda.
